summary: A note from Robert Kahn about a computer communication network demonstration he was organizing for the International Computer Communications Conference in Washington on 24 to 26 October 1972. The demonstration would run alongside the conference sessions and show network use.

eli5.summary: A scientist is setting up a booth at a big meeting to show visitors how computers can talk to each other across the country.

subtitle: Plans for the ARPANET demonstration at the International Computer Communications Conference.

tldr.problem: The emerging field of computer communications was new to most people and needed public visibility and demonstration to show its value.
tldr.mechanism: Robert Kahn organized a live demonstration of the ARPANET for the International Computer Communications Conference scheduled for October 1972 in Washington, D.C., showing real use cases like database retrieval and resource sharing.
tldr.outcome: The demonstration would give conference attendees hands-on experience with a working computer network and demonstrate practical applications.

today: RFC 371 documents an important moment in ARPANET history when researchers worked to demonstrate the network's value to the broader computing community, laying groundwork for the public understanding of networking technology.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 371 is an invitation from Robert Kahn at BBN to the ARPANET community to help organize and staff a network demonstration at the International Computer Communications Conference. The conference, scheduled for 24 to 26 October 1972 at the Washington, D.C. Hilton Hotel, would address issues in computer communications with about 17 sessions covering social, educational and business implications.
sections.eli5: A big conference about computer networks was coming up, and someone wanted to show everyone how the ARPANET actually works in real time.

sections.title: The Demonstration Concept
sections.content: Kahn describes the theme of the demo: showing the value of computer communication networks. It would emphasize practical benefits such as database retrieval, combined use of multiple machines, real-time data access, interactive cooperation and simulation systems. The plan was to deliver a TIP to the Hilton Hotel and connect it to the ARPANET, allowing all terminals in the ballroom to access both ARPANET resources and non-ARPANET resources temporarily connected for the demonstration.
sections.eli5: The demo would show what you can do with a network: look up information in databases, use computers in different places at the same time, run simulations, and work with people remotely.

sections.title: Preparation and Outreach
sections.content: Kahn explains that significant effort was being devoted to making the demonstration easy for novice users. The NIC and others were creating clear documentation so people could sit down and effectively use selected resources without assistance. Kahn calls for help from network sites, stressing that the effort is large and requires time and energy from the community. He gives his contact information and invites suggestions from anyone involved or interested.
sections.eli5: Lots of work was needed to make it easy for visitors who had never used a network to sit down and try it out. The organizer asked for help from everyone in the network community.
